title: Utility Order for Cleco Power LLC and Pine JV Holdings LLC. — Order No. U37963 approves the change of ownership of Cleco Power LLC, subject to commitments. This matter was considered at the November 18, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                      ORDER NUMBER U-37963

                    CLECO POWER LLC AND PINE JV HOLDINGS LLC.

Docket No. U-37963, In re: Joint application of Cleco Power LLC and Pine JV Holdings LLC
for authorization for the change of ownership and control of Cleco Power LLC.

             (Decided at the November 18, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)
I.      Overview

        Cleco Power, LLC, and Pine JV Holdings, LLC, together (“Joint Applicants”) filed the

application in this matter on June 16, 2026 (“Application”), which was noticed in the Louisiana

Public Service Commission’s (“LPSC” or the “Commission”) Official Bulletin No. 1378, issued

June 18, 2026. Timely interventions were filed by the Alliance for Affordable Energy (“AAE”),

Sierra Club, and Packaging Corporation of America (“PCA”). Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”),

Cabot Corporation (“Cabot”), and the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”)

requested interested party status. The Joint Applicants have requested Commission authorization

of the change of ownership and control of Cleco Power, which would result in Pine JV Holdings

acquiring from Cleco Partners L.P. 100% of the ownership interest of Cleco Group LLC, which

currently holds 100% of the ownership interest of Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC (“Cleco

Corporate Holdings”), which in turn currently holds 100% of the ownership interest of Cleco

Power (the “Transaction”).

        Joint Applicants urged that the proposed Transaction satisfies the 18-factor public interest

test set forth in the LPSC General Order dated March 18, 1994 (the “1994 General Order”).

Further, the Application included a set of regulatory commitments that the Joint Applicants

proposed be carried forward from Cleco Power’s prior change of ownership and control

proceeding that the Commission authorized in LPSC Order No. U-33434-A, issued April 7, 2016.1

The Application was supported by the Direct Testimonies of William Fontenont, President and

Chief Executive Officer of Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC, Kristin Guillory, Chief Financial

Officer of Cleco Corporate Holdings, and Mark Kleehammer, General Counsel and Chief

Regulatory Officer of Cleco Corporate Holdings, on behalf of Cleco Power, and Rob Kupchak,

Senior Managing Director at Stonepeak Partners LP (“Stonepeak”), and Jeff Baudier, Senior

Managing Director at Bernhard Capital Partners Management, LP (“BCP”), on behalf of Pine JV



1 Docket No. U-34434, Cleco Power LLC, ex parte. In re: Joint Application of Cleco Power LLC and Cleco Partners

L.P. for: (1) Authorization for the Change of Ownership and Control of Cleco Power LLC and (ii) Expedited
Treatment.

                                                                                        Order No. U-37963
                                                                                                   Page 1
 Holdings. Pine JV Holdings is a Delaware limited liability company formed for the purpose of

this transaction. Its investors are Stonepeak Partners LP (75% interest) and Bernhard Capital

Partners Management LP (25% interest). Stonepeak is a global infrastructure investment firm

headquartered in New York City, and Bernhard is a market services and infrastructure-focused

private equity investment firm headquartered in Baton Rouge.

        The proposed Transaction is an upstream, like-kind change in the ownership of Cleco

Power that is designed to leave in place Cleco Power’s current quality and reliability of service,

retail rate structure, senior management, employees, and connections with Louisiana and Cleco

Power’s service territory, with comparable financial backing, commitments, and financial risk.

The current majority owner’s fund is approaching the planned end of its investment term, and Pine

JV Holdings proposed to step into substantially the same regulatory commitments that currently

govern Cleco Power and the current owners. To consummate the Transaction, Pine JV Holdings

would acquire 100% of the issued and outstanding limited liability company member interests of

Cleco Group through an Equity Purchase Agreement (“Purchase Agreement”) and would step into

the existing capital structure and indebtedness levels of Cleco Group.

       After extensive formal and informal discovery and analysis, on October 23, 2026, the

LPSC Staff filed the Direct Testimony and Exhibits of R. Lane Sisung and the Direct Testimony

of John E. Mayeaux. Staff recommended that the proposed transfer of functional control meets

the overall public interest requirements of the 1994 General Order if certain proposed conditions

set forth in those direct testimonies are adopted. Factor 11 of the 1994 General Order specifically

allows for the adoption of conditions necessary to prevent adverse consequences that may result

from the proposed transfer.

       After direct testimony was filed, the Applicants indicated general agreement with Staff’s

conclusions and proposed amended Commitments, but had questions and concerns regarding some

of the amended Commitments. After some discussions, the questions were answered and the

concerns were consensually resolved.         An Uncontested Proposed Stipulated Settlement

(“Stipulation”) was prepared and executed on November 12, 2026. It is supported by the

Applicants and Staff, and it is unopposed by the remaining parties to this proceeding, PCA, the

AAE, and Sierra Club, and resolves all issues in this proceeding.

       On November 12, 2026, Joint Applicants filed an Unopposed Joint Motion for

Consideration by the Commission Pursuant to Rule 57 and approval of Uncontested Proposed


                                                                              Order No. U-37963
                                                                                         Page 2
 Stipulated Settlement. The Settlement was supported by the Settlement Testimony of Cleco Power

witness Mark Kleehammer, the Settlement Testimony of Pine JV Holdings witnesses Rob

Kubchak and Jeff Baudier, and the Settlement Testimony of Commission Staff witness R.

Lane Sisung. The matter was included on the agenda of the October 22, 2026 Business and

Executive Session for Commission consideration.

II.       COMMISSION JURISDICTION

          The Commission's authority and jurisdiction are specifically set forth in Article IV Section

21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which sets forth in pertinent part:

          The Commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and shall
          have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and enforce
          reasonable rules, regulations and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
          duties, and perform other duties as provided by law.

III.      STIPULATED SETTLEMENT

          A.      PUBLIC INTEREST DETERMINATION; REGULATORY
                  COMMITMENTS; NO OPPOSITION

       1. Public Interest Determination.
          Subject to the terms and conditions of this Settlement, the Joint Applicants and the
          Commission Staff agree that the proposed Transaction for the change of ownership and
          control of Cleco Power satisfies the 18-factor test specified in the 1994 General Order, is
          in the public interest, and should be authorized by the Commission. The Intervenors each
          express no opposition to the proposed Transaction.

       2. Regulatory Commitments.
          The Joint Applicants and the Commission Staff have agreed upon a set of regulatory
          commitments that would be effective immediately upon the closing of the proposed
          Transaction (the “New Regulatory Commitments”), should the Commission determine that
          the proposed Transaction is in the public interest. A copy of the New Regulatory
          Commitments is attached hereto as Exhibit A. The Joint Applicants and the Commission
          Staff agree that the New Regulatory Commitments are in the public interest, should be
          authorized by the Commission, and, if the Commission authorizes the Transaction, should
          be attached to the Commission’s authorizing order. The Intervenors each express no
          opposition to the New Regulatory Commitments.

       3. No Opposition to this Settlement.
          Subject to the terms and conditions of this Settlement and the reservation of rights
          described in Section III(B) below, each Intervenor acknowledges and agrees that it has no
          opposition to this Settlement.


          B.      GENERAL PROVISIONS

       1. The Commission order issued in this proceeding shall be effective immediately upon its
          date of issuance.

       2. Except as specifically stated herein, this Settlement shall have no precedential effect in
          any other proceeding and shall be without prejudice to the right of any party to take any
          position in future proceedings or appeals therefrom. The terms of this Settlement may not


                                                                                 Order No. U-37963
                                                                                            Page 3
        be used either as an admission of any sort or as evidence in any proceeding whatsoever,
       except to approve or enforce the terms of this Settlement.

   3. This Settlement will be effective upon authorization by the Commission. The Parties agree
      to request Commission authorization of this Settlement at the November 18, 2026,
      Business & Executive Meeting.


IV. COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

       This matter was considered by the Commission at its November 18, 2026 Business and

Executive Session.     After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by

Commissioner Francis, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to take the matter up

pursuant to Rule 57 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of this Commission, and on motion of

Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, and unanimously adopted, the

Commission voted to accept the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on

November 12, 2026.

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

       1. The Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on November 12, 2026 is
          accepted, with a copy of the New Regulatory Commitments attached hereto as
          Attachment A.

       2. This order is effective immediately.



BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 24, 2026


                                         /S/ ERIC F. SKRMETTA
                                         DISTRICT I
                                         CHAIRMAN ERIC F. SKRMETTA

                                         /S/ JEAN-PAUL P. COUSSAN
                                         DISTRICT II
                                         VICE CHAIRMAN JEAN-PAUL P. COUSSAN

                                         DISTRICT V

 SECRETARY

                    ATTACHMENT A

STAFF’S PROPOSED REVISIONS TO REGULATORY COMMITMENTS
                                 REGULATORY COMMITMENTS



Enforcement and Compliance

1.    Cleco Power LLC ("Cleco Power"), as an electric public utility, will remain jurisdictional to the
      Louisiana Public Service Commission ("LPSC" or "Commission"), as it is now. Each of the New
      Owners requesting approval of the LPSC to purchase all of the ownership interests of Cleco Group
      LLC ("Cleco Group"), being Pine JV Holdings LLC, Pine JV Aggregator LP, SP Pine Upper
      Holdings LP and Pine Utilities Holdco, LP, for the sole purpose of holding the ownership interests,
      indirectly, in Pine JV Holdings LLC (each, a "New Owner" and, collectively, the "New Owners")
      as well as Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC (“Cleco Corporate Holdings”), Cleco
      Group and New Owners agree to fully and in good faith support the implementation of all
      commitments herein of Cleco Corporate Holdings and Cleco Power and more specifically are
      obligated to take all steps necessary to allow Cleco Power and Cleco Corporate Holdings to fully
      comply with each of these commitments and to that end, to act consistently with, facilitate, and not
      interfere with the implementation of all commitments herein of Cleco Corporate Holdings and
      Cleco Power. Nothing herein, however, will serve to create Commission jurisdiction over Cleco
      Corporate Holdings, Cleco Group, or any of the New Owners, except to enforce the obligations as
      agreed to herein. Notwithstanding the foregoing, each of Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate Holdings,
      Cleco Group, and each New Owner agrees, to the extent this set of regulatory commitments creates
      an obligation as part of a regulatory commitment, and one or more of them is in breach thereof, that
      the Commission may seek to compel specific performance of said obligation or otherwise utilize
      injunctive relief against such particular obligor(s) who undertook said obligation before the
      Commission, the FERC, or a court of competent jurisdiction. Each of Cleco Power, Cleco
      Corporate Holdings, Cleco Group, and each New Owner agrees that in seeking to invoke the use
      of specific performance or injunctive relief, the Commission will not be required to demonstrate:
      1) that irreparable harm, loss or damage will be suffered, absent the issuance of the injunction; 2)
      the lack of an adequate remedy at law or in damages; 3) that injunctive relief is necessary in the
      public interest; or 4) that the balance of harm favors the Commission. Further, each of Cleco Power,
      Cleco Corporate Holdings, Cleco Group, and each New Owner agrees, to the extent this set of
      regulatory commitments creates an obligation as part of a regulatory commitment, and one or more
      of them is in breach thereof, that it waives any objection based upon the Commission's lack of
      jurisdiction over it to the Commission's seeking such specific performance or injunctive relief.
      Further, Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate Holdings, Cleco Group and each New Owner consents to
      jurisdiction and venue in Louisiana State Court to the extent necessary to enforce the regulatory
      commitments via specific performance or injunction. Each of Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate
      Holdings, Cleco Group, and each New Owner, in connection with such requested specific
      performance or injunctive relief, retains the right to demonstrate that it has not committed to an
      obligation as part of a regulatory commitment or that it is not in breach of such obligation.

2.    Cleco Power acknowledges that all existing orders issued by the Commission with respect to Cleco
      Power or its predecessors will remain in effect, and are not modified or otherwise affected by the
      Transaction or any order of the Commission authorizing the Transaction, except and unless
      specifically and expressly provided in the Commission's final order authorizing the Transaction.

3.    Cleco Power will continue to comply with all Commission-issued orders and rules applicable to
      Cleco Power. Cleco Power will comply with all applicable Commission orders and rules issued in


                                                   2
        the future. Cleco Power agrees that it will not contest the Commission's jurisdiction over its retail
       rates and provision of service. Cleco Power, whenever and wherever appropriate, will make timely
       and compliant filings with the Commission in accordance with the Commission's rules and orders
       applicable to Cleco Power. Cleco Power's obligations in these regards are in no way diminished
       by the Transaction or any order of the Commission authorizing the Transaction. Cleco Power's
       compliance obligations before the Commission are subject to Cleco Power's full procedural rights
       before the Commission and rights of judicial review.

4.     Cleco Power acknowledges that its Commission jurisdictional rates are specified in the overall
       retail rate-setting determinations, including Order No. U-36923, issued July 17, 2024, as well as
       Cleco Power's Third Amended Formula Rate Plan ("FRP") effective for the periods July 1, 2025
       through June 30, 2026 and July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Cleco Power will continue to
       comply with all requirements and obligations of the Commission's rate-setting orders.
       Accordingly, Cleco Power shall continue to make annual rate filings pursuant to the current
       Formula Rate Plan. Cleco Power also acknowledges that certain of its fuel and fuel-related costs
       are recoverable under its Fuel Adjustment Clause pursuant to the Commission's FAC General Order
       of November 6, 1997. Cleco Power also specifically commits not to apply to adjust its compliance
       obligations under that general order, except as already permitted in the general order, including but
       not limited to its Subsections IV(M) (Exceptions) and IV(N) (Treatment of Exceptions or
       Uncertainties). Unless expressly resolved in these commitments, no ratemaking issues are resolved
       herein and the parties reserve their rights with respect to such ratemaking issues in any future
       proceedings before the Commission.

5.     Neither Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate Holdings nor Cleco Group will advocate for a higher cost
       of debt or equity capital as compared to what Cleco Power's cost of debt or equity would have been
       absent the Transaction.

Organizational and Operational Continuities

6.     Cleco Power and Cleco Corporate Holdings will both remain Louisiana entities and both shall have
       their corporate headquarters remain in Pineville, Louisiana. Should Cleco Power or Cleco
       Corporate Holdings seek to relocate its corporate headquarters outside of Pineville, Louisiana, it
       will provide the Commission with a minimum of eighteen (18) months' notice. Cleco Power and
       Cleco Corporate Holdings are prohibited from relocating their corporate headquarters outside of
       Pineville, Louisiana, without formal Commission approval (i.e., by a majority vote of the
       Commission).

7.     Cleco Power and Cleco Corporate Holdings, as the parent company of Cleco Support Group, will
       maintain staffing and presence in the communities in which Cleco Power operates at levels
       sufficient to maintain the provision of safe and reliable service and efficient operations.

       The New Owners, Cleco Group LLC, and Cleco Corporate Holdings agree to support and ensure
       Cleco Power’s compliance with a Commission-approved Service Quality Program (“SQP”) for at
       least five (5) years following closing of the Transaction. The terms and conditions of that program
       shall be established by the Commission in its order in Docket No. U-37969.

       Until the SQP established by the Commission in Docket No. U-37969 becomes effective, Cleco
       Power shall maintain and comply with the Service Quality Program incorporated as Attachment B
       to Order No. U-33434-A, issued April 7, 2016, including its attached exhibits and any subsequent


                                                    3
      modifications expressly authorized by the Commission. Notwithstanding expiration of that
     program’s original term, its requirements shall remain binding during this interim period. The
     filing or pendency of a proposed replacement or amendment shall not alter these interim
     obligations.

     The SQP , or any modifications or replacement authorized by the Commission in Docket No. U-
     37969, will remain in effect for five (5) years after the closing of the Transaction; provided,
     however, that the ten (10) year terms specified in Commitment 8 and Commitment 11 will survive
     beyond the five (5) year initial term of the SQP. Prior to the expiration of the five (5) year term of
     the SQP, a new five (5) year SQP must be negotiated and submitted to the Commission for
     approval.

8.   With respect to all employees (approximately 1,200 in total), including those employees covered
     under the SQP, Cleco Power and Cleco Support Group will maintain employee headcount, salaries,
     and benefits substantially consistent with or higher than current levels in the aggregate across Cleco
     Power and Cleco Support Group for at least ten (10) years following closing of the Transaction.
     Employee headcounts may not drop more than two (2) percent from current levels, (including the
     benchmarks described in the SQP). The commitment to maintain headcounts does not mean that
     any particular individual is guaranteed to keep his or her job. Cleco Power and Cleco Support
     Group have the right to expect their employees to continue to operate according to the highest
     standards. Cleco Power and Cleco Support Group retain the right to terminate employees without
     cause or for cause. To the extent that Cleco Power seeks to permanently eliminate any employee
     positions (i.e., not individuals) or functions or seeks to permanently outsource or automate any
     functions beyond the threshold specified above within that ten (10) year period, the proposed
     change must be submitted to the Commission at least 120 days in advance of the proposed change;
     provided, however, that the foregoing requirement shall not apply to, and shall not impair, Cleco
     Power's ability to utilize the netting mechanism established and defined in Article XII of the SQP.
     Such notification shall include the proposed date of the change, the reasons for the change, the
     expected cost savings from the change, the manner in which those cost savings will be flowed
     through to ratepayers, the relocation of the impacted employees, if any, and the anticipated impact
     on Cleco Power's reliability and quality of service. No such change shall be made without formal
     Commission authorization (i.e., by a majority vote of the Commission).

9.   In the event Cleco proposes any change in the organizational structure of Cleco's field personnel
     workforce, resulting in a permanent reduction of the total number of field personnel workforce
     below the baseline set forth in the SQP, (including, but not limited to, reduced employee levels
     attributable to layoffs, outsourcing and/or additional reliance on contract personnel), Cleco shall
     make a filing with the Commission at least 120 days in advance of the proposed change, describing
     all proposed changes, the reasons for said modifications or reduction, the expected cost savings
     from such a change and the manner in which those cost savings will be flowed through to
     ratepayers. No such change shall be made without affirmative Commission approval. This does
     not preclude Cleco from "netting" positions. "Netting" is defined as eliminating one employee
     position for efficiency purposes and filling a comparable position in another area of the Company
     to meet a specific need. Upon receipt of the filing, the Commission may take all appropriate actions
     to ensure that proposed management or employee changes do not adversely affect the provision,
     reliability, and cost of service to Louisiana customers. If retail access is mandated by the
     Commission, or through action by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or federal or state
     legislation, the Company must submit any proposed management changes to the Commission no
     less than 120 days in advance of the effective date of such changes.


                                                   4
 10.   As part of the Transaction, Cleco Power intends to retain current senior management to the extent
      those individuals agree to that retention. This commitment will not limit the ability of Cleco Power,
      subject to the provisions of the SQP, to determine its organizational structure and select and retain
      personnel best able to meet Cleco Power's needs over time.

11.   There will be no adverse material change in Cleco Power's pension plans or pension design or in
      current benefits for retiree medical plan participants for at least ten (10) years.

12.   Cleco Power and Cleco Corporate Holdings, as the parent company of Cleco Support Group, will
      maintain or increase the existing level of corporate contributions and community support in
      Louisiana, which may include the establishment of a charitable foundation to make charitable
      contributions within Louisiana consistent with Cleco Power's and Cleco Corporate Holdings's
      current practices.

13.   Cleco Power and Cleco Corporate Holdings, as the parent company of Cleco Support Group, will
      maintain a level of economic development funding of no less than $760,000 annually for Louisiana
      state and local organizations for at least five (5) years following the closing of the Transaction. In
      addition, Cleco Corporate Holdings and Cleco Power shall make a one-time contribution in an
      amount of $10 million to a fund to be administered by the Louisiana Department of Economic
      Development, or other agency of the state of Louisiana, or such other public interest entity
      acceptable to the Commission, for the purpose of financially supporting capital costs of economic
      development projects located within Cleco Power's service area. The one-time contribution shall
      not count toward the annual funding minimum required by this commitment.

14.   Cleco Power commits to continue the reliability and quality of service measures currently in place
      for Cleco Power or as may be modified in this or in any other future Commission proceeding. To
      this end, Cleco Power will maintain its customer call center in Pineville, Louisiana for a minimum
      of five (5) years and also will maintain management of generation, transmission, distribution, retail
      sales, and storm restoration in Louisiana. If Cleco Power determines that a call center is no longer
      the most efficient means to handle communications with its customers, and Cleco Power desires to
      replace the current call center with some other system, then Cleco Power must file with the
      Commission, at least six (6) months prior to the date of any such proposed change, a detailed
      description of the proposed system, the reasons the proposed system is believed to be more efficient
      than the call center, the net difference in cost of the proposed system, and the anticipated impact
      on Cleco Power's ability to receive, process, and address customer communications. The
      Commission will utilize its best efforts to rule within 120 days of such a filing, on whether Cleco
      Power may replace the call center with the new system; provided, however, that the foregoing
      requirement shall not apply to, and shall not impair, Cleco Power from "netting" positions as
      defined in Commitment No. 9. Further, Cleco Power will maintain or improve its current capital
      investment, operating and maintenance and procurement practices. Also, Cleco Power's current
      pole replacement and vegetation management practices will be continued or improved in order to
      maintain service reliability. Cleco Power will continue to actively participate in national and
      regional forums regarding best utility practices in all significant areas of Cleco Power's operations
      and incorporate such best utility practices as determined to be reasonably appropriate by Cleco
      Power, subject to any Commission review allowed by law. In addition, Cleco Power will comply
      with the SQP, including ongoing adjustments pursuant to the provisions of this paragraph as may
      be made appropriate under the SQP.




                                                    5
 15.          Cleco Power commits to maintain its existing (or a comparable), voluntary low-income assistance
             program, i.e., its Cleco Alternative Rate for Electricity (CARE), for a minimum of five (5) years
             following the closing of the Transaction.

Officers and Directors

16.          For a minimum of five (5) years from the close of the Transaction, Cleco Group's chief executive
             officer, senior management responsible for Cleco Power's operations (e.g., generation, distribution,
             transmission, regulatory and commercial), and senior management of corporate support functions
             (e.g., financial, human resources, and legal) will have their principal places of residence in
             Louisiana.

17.          (a)      A minimum of four (4) directors of Cleco Group's board will have their principal places of
             residence in Louisiana, with one (1) of those four (4) being the chairman and one (1) of those four
             (4) being the chief executive officer. 1 The chief executive officer of Cleco Group will also serve
             on the boards of Cleco Corporate Holdings and Cleco Power. The affirmative vote of at least one
             of the Louisiana resident directors, except the Chief Executive Officer of Cleco Power, shall be
             required for all resolutions of the boards of Cleco Group, Cleco Corporate Holdings or Cleco Power
             to be effective. The votes of the individual directors on all resolutions adopted by such boards shall
             be recorded and such voting records shall be available on request to the Commission.

             (b)      Subject to general supervision of the board of directors, including the New Owners'
             directors and Louisiana resident directors, Cleco Power's senior management shall have full
             authority to manage the daily operations of Cleco Power in full accordance with its commitments
             and obligations herein and with its public service obligations generally, and specifically with
             respect to the management of storm and other emergency responses and related service restorations.

Economic and Financial

18.          Cleco Power will not seek, nor will the Commission authorize recovery of any Transaction-related
             costs or costs incurred after the Transaction closes that are caused or required by the Transaction,
             whether internal or external and which would be in addition to those costs that would be borne by
             Cleco Power absent the Transaction. These include costs incurred in connection with seeking
             approvals from the Commission and/or any other regulatory, governmental or quasi-governmental
             authority for the Transaction. Without limitation, there will be no rate recovery, directly or
             indirectly, by Cleco Power of legal and financial advisory fees associated with the Transaction, no
             rate recovery of the acquisition premium, no rate recovery of regulatory costs, and no rate recovery
             of any executive change-of-control or severance compensation of any kind, including medical
             obligations, as a result of the Transaction.

19.          Cleco Power will issue and maintain its own debt and preferred stock (if any) pursuant to the
             Commission's existing blanket financing authorization for Cleco Power or pursuant to any
             supplementary or superseding financing authorizations by the Commission.


1     For purposes of this regulatory commitment no. 17, each of the resident directors, other than the CEO, shall be an individual who (i) is not a representative of or advisor to
      Cleco Power, Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC, Cleco Group, the Joint Applicants, or any affiliate of any of the foregoing named entities; (ii) is not, and has not been within
      the last three (3) years, an employee of any of the foregoing named entities or any of their affiliates; and (iii) has no ownership interest in any of the foregoing named entities
      or any of their affiliates.




                                                                                          6
 20.    Cleco Power commits to maintain investment grade credit ratings with two (2) of Moody's Investors
       Service, Standard & Poor's Ratings Services, or Fitch Ratings and, further, will seek to improve
       such credit ratings over time. Nothing in these commitments will limit the Commission's authority
       to set rates or establish conditions to protect ratepayers from the consequences of any potential
       credit downgrades resulting from the Transaction, and Cleco Power commits to hold ratepayers
       harmless from any increase in the cost of debt to Cleco Power caused by such potential credit
       downgrades. Cleco Power shall provide notice to the Commission of any changes to the credit
       rating of Cleco Power within five (5) business days of Cleco Power's receipt of notice of such
       change to the credit rating.

21.    Cleco Power is not requesting in this proceeding a determination of the prudence, just and
       reasonable character, rate or ratemaking treatment, or public interest of the investments,
       expenditures or actions referenced in these regulatory commitments (but for the Transaction, itself),
       and the parties in appropriate proceedings may take such positions regarding the prudence, just and
       reasonable character, rate or ratemaking treatment, or public interest of the investments,
       expenditures or actions as they deem appropriate. However, to the extent that the Commission does
       make determinations regarding certain Transaction-related issues (e.g., the requirement that all
       costs of the Transaction must be borne by shareholders, not ratepayers), those determinations are
       final and determinative in future proceedings.

22.    Cleco Power shall use alternative financing strategies pursuant to Act 64 and or Act 55 to address
       substantial storm damage (and reserves) unless it is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the
       Commission that another methodology of financing storm damages and reserves is a less costly
       option.

23.    New Owners shall obtain an opinion letter that the Transaction: (a) would not cause Cleco to be in
       violation of Commission Order No. U-35807-A (Hurricanes Laura, Delta and Zeta and Winter
       Storms Uri and Viola); (b) would not cause Cleco to be in violation of Act 64 of the Louisiana
       Legislature of 2006; (c) would not cause Cleco Power to be in violation of Commission Order No.
       U-35807-B; and (d) would not jeopardize any terms of the bonds sold pursuant to Commission
       Order No. U-35807-B. Further, Cleco Power will obtain an opinion letter that the Transaction: (a)
       would not cause Cleco to be in violation of Commission Order No. U-37213 (Dolet Hills Power
       Station and Associated Mines); (b) would not cause Cleco to be in violation of the Louisiana
       Electric Utility Energy Transaction Securitization Act (La. R.S. 45:1271-1281); and (c) would not
       jeopardize any terms of the bonds sold pursuant to Commission Order No. U-37213.

Ring-Fencing and Inter-Affiliate Accounting and Conduct

24.    Cleco Power will maintain separate books, records, and documents so as to provide an audit trail
       to the Commission for all affiliate transactions of Cleco Power and all activities of Cleco Power
       that may result in affiliate costs that may be allocable to Cleco Power. Any affiliate transactions
       of Cleco Power, and all activities of Cleco Power, that may result in affiliate costs should be
       adequately documented and performed to comply with the Commission's affiliate rules made
                                                                      2
       applicable to Cleco Power in the Commission's Red Simpson order.




2
       Red Simpson, Inc. v. Cleco Corporation, Order No. U-24064, dated Nov. 20, 2000 (“Red Simpson”).



                                                    7
 25.   Cleco Power will provide the Commission access to Cleco Power's and Cleco Corporate Holdings's
      books, records, and documents, as well as their employees, officers and directors (collectively
      "personnel"), as well as any other information required to be accessed by the Commission to verify
      or examine affiliate transactions of Cleco Power and all activities of Cleco Power that may result
      in affiliate costs that may be allocable to Cleco Power. That access will remain available for the

74.   Sponsor-Related Affiliate Transactions.

      For purposes of these Regulatory Commitments and the application of the Commission’s affiliate-
      transaction protections, a “Covered Entity” means Stonepeak, BCP, each New Owner, and any
      entity other than Cleco Power and its subsidiaries, that (i) is directly or indirectly controlled or
      managed by Stonepeak, BCP, any New Owner, or any of their controlled or managed investment
      funds or entities or (ii) is at least twenty (20) percent owned, directly or indirectly and in the
      aggregate, by those parties, measured by equity ownership or rights to profits. Control and
      management mean decision-making authority over an entity’s operations, investments, or policies,
      whether exercised through ownership, contractual rights, appointment rights, or otherwise; advice
      alone is insufficient to establish either. An investment below the twenty (20) percent threshold
      does not, by itself, establish coverage where no qualifying control or management relationship
      exists. Covered Entities include investment funds, co-investment vehicles, portfolio companies,
      and joint ventures meeting this definition.

      Transactions between Cleco Power and a Covered Entity shall be treated as affiliate transactions
      for purposes of these Regulatory Commitments and the Commission’s applicable affiliate rules and
      orders, regardless of whether the Covered Entity otherwise satisfies a definition of affiliate. This
      requirement includes transactions conducted through an intermediary or project entity where a
      Covered Entity participates in the arrangement or receives compensation attributable to it.

      The New Owners shall provide Cleco Power with current information sufficient to identify Covered
      Entities involved in transactions or continuing agreements with Cleco Power. Cleco Power shall
      disclose each such entity and the ownership, investment, or management relationship giving rise to
      its coverage in the notices and filings required by this commitment and in an annual filing updating
      that information. The annual filing shall supplement, and shall not replace, the transaction-specific
      notices required by this commitment.

      Cleco Power shall provide written notice to the Commission within (30) days after entering into a
      binding agreement for a transaction covered by the commitment, including a binding commitment
      of fund assets or services. Notice shall identify the parties and their relationships; describe the
      transaction, its purpose, and material economic terms; identify any utility contributions,
      obligations, guarantees, or other financial support; and explain the affiliate pricing, procurement,
      allocation, and other protections proposed to apply. The notice requirement applies to purchases
      and sales of goods or services, construction, fuel and transportation arrangements, financing, leases,
      asset transfers, electric-service arrangements, joint ventures, and material amendments to such
      arrangements. The agreement’s effectiveness need not be deferred solely to provide notice under
      this commitment. Any separate requirement for prior Commission approval remains fully
      applicable. Any alternative notice procedure or exception shall require express Commission
      authorization.

      Covered transactions shall comply with the Commission’s applicable affiliate pricing, competitive-
      procurement, cost-allocation, accounting, and cross-subsidization requirements, including
      applicable requirements of Order No. U-24064, the Commission’s Market Based Mechanisms
